 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident caused on 12.01.2020.
02.

The brief facts of the petition is as under: It is submitted that on 12.01.2020 at about 04.30 p.m when the petitioner was proceeding on his Motor Cycle bearing No.AP03AN0475 on the extreme left side of road and when he reached near Kutalavanka Cross, on Baireddipally  V.Kota Road, Baireddipally (SCCH3) 3 M.V.C.No.1012/20 Mandal, at that time a Lorry bearing No. TN 70AB6189 came in rash and negligent manner from opposite direction and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to this impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to PES hospital, Kuppam and after first aid he was shifted to Sparsh hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgeries and below knee was amputed under GA.

The petitioner had spent more than Rs.15,00,000/
towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
The petitioner prior to the accident was hale and healthy and was doing agricultural work and vegetable business and earning Rs.40,000/ per month.
Due to amputation of right leg, he could not able to continue his work and sustained disability and suffered financial loss.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the offending lorry driver only.
Even a criminal case is registered against the said lorry driver.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the said lorry.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence this petition.

(SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.1012/20 03. After service of notice, the respondent No.2 had not appeared before this court on the date fixed for their appearance and hence they were placed absent through out the proceedings of the petition.

However the respondent No.1 have appeared through their counsel and filed written statement.
04.
The averments of the written statement of the respondent No.1 are as under : The respondent No.2 has not intimated about the accident.
The petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties.
This respondent has issued the policy in favour of the respondent No.2 which is valid from 08.05.2019 to 07.05.2020.
But liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
At the time of accident the lorry has no fitness certificate and the lorry driver does not hold valid driving licence.
Hence the respondent No.2 has violated the terms of the policy.
The offending lorry was not involved in the accident.
The accident took place due to the negligence of petitioner himself.
At the time of accident the petitioner had not wore helmet or did not possessed valid driving licence.
It is denied that due to the accident the petitioner has sustained disability and lost income as stated in the petition.

This respondent has denied the manner of accident, injuries and (SCCH3) 5 Sri.C.Subramanyam vs The New India Assurance on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54107932/
2 M.V.C.No.1012/20 income as stated by the petitioner.

sentences.text: This petition was filed in collusion with police and respondent No.2 in order to make unlawful gain.
The claim of the petitioner is exorbitant and prays to dismiss petition with costs.
05. In order to prove the case, the petitioner and doctor were examined themselves as PW.1 and 2 and got marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 16 and closed his side.
06. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.1 inspite of providing several opportunity did not adduced any evidence.

07. Heard both sides.
08.
Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:

01. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 12.01.2020 at about 04.30 p.m, near Kutalavanka Cross, on Baireddipalli  V.Kota Road,
Baireddipalli Mandal, due to rash and negligent act of the driving of the Lorry bearing reg. No.TN 70AB6189 by its driver as alleged in the petition ?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount & from whom?
( SCCH3
. What order or award?

09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under: Issue No.1 : In affirmative Issue No.2 : In partly affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the grievance of the petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of lorry driver bearing No.TN70AB6189.
Due to the accident he had sustained disability and lost income.
The same was opposed by the respondent No.1 and contended that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of offending lorry driver and it is due to the negligence of petitioner himself.
The insured vehicle is falsely implicated in this case in order to claim compensation.
Hence they are not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
11. To prove this, the petitioner was got examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
The PW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that "That I was (SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.1012/20 proceeding on two wheeler alone.
When he was going upwards the lorry came from downwards in wrong side and dashed to me.
It is true that in this accident the lorry driver died.
There is no divider in the accident road.
That the rod was inserted over the hip region.
I had not produced any document to show that I was earning Rs.40,000/ per month.

That I had Sri.C.Subramanyam vs The New India Assurance on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54107932/
3 already purchased artificial limb".

sentences.text: Apart from this the PW.1 had denied other suggestion of the respondent No.1 counsel.
12. The PW.1 in support of his case got marked entire police documents at Ex.P.1 to 6.

So on perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation has filed abated chargesheet against the offending lorry driver for the alleged offences punishable U/Sec 338 and 304(a) of IPC stating that the petitioner had sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of offending lorry driver only.

13. It is true that eventhough the respondent No.1 contended that the accident does not took place due to their insured lorry driver, but to prove this they have not adduced any supportive oral and documentary evidence.
Even the mahazar and other police records got marked supports the version of the petitioner.

So on perusal of all police records (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.1012/20 accompanied with the oral evidence of the PW.1 and in absence of rebuttal evidence by the respondent No.1 in this regard, it is true that the petitioner has proved that the offending lorry was involved in this accident and its driver due to his negligent driving had caused the accident which leads to injuries to him.

14. Therefore with the available oral and documentary evidence, it is true that the petitioner has proved that he had sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry driver.
Hence I answered the issue No.1 in affirmative.
15. Issue No.2: Further the petitioner has stated that due to the accident he is not able to do work as earlier and sustained disability.

In this regard he had got examined the Orthopedic Surgeon as PW.2 who had stated that petitioner had sustained total amputation of the right foot, fracture of right distal tibia and fibula, fracture of right femur, right 10 th rib fracture and multiple laceration over the face.
16. That as per the recent xray it reveals that united fracture of the right femur with implant in situ and right leg shows evidence of below knee amputation.

The petitioner complains of unable to walk,
need support, severe pain in the right hip and knee.

The PW.2 had assessed below knee amputation of 70% and stump and unstable painful of 10% and in total he had assessed 80%
disability.

The PW.2 has got marked case sheet and Xray as per Ex.P.15 and 16.
18.
The PW.2 in his cross examination has admitted that "That I am one in the team which treated the petitioner.
The amputation was done on 13.01.2020.
The petitioner had total amputation of the right foot with fracture of tibia and fibula, hence amputation was done below knee.
It is true that as amputation is done there is no difficulty to do job by sitting.
It is true that the fracture of right femur is united.
It is true that the rib fracture is united.

It is true that I had assessed the disability for all Sri.C.Subramanyam vs The New India Assurance on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54107932/
4 injuries".

sentences.text: 19. The counsel for petitioner has relied upon decision in Civil Appeal No.2567/2020 - Pappu Deo Yadav V/s Naresh Kumar and others  wherein it was observed that when there is permanent disability then future prospects to be awarded.

entities.text: Pappu Deo Yadav V/s Naresh Kumar and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. But the above observation is not applicable to the facts of this case as in the instant case there is no total and permanent disability.
Hence, from the evidence of PW.2 and from Ex.P.15 and 16, the petitioner has sustained disability due to the accident, (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.1012/20 but not as stated by the PW.2.
It is true that the petitioner has undergone amputation.
It is true that the petitioner has stated that he is doing agricultural work and by sitting he could not carry out any agricultural work.
However by sitting he can do vegetable selling business.
Hence as contended by the petitioner the disability of the petitioner could not be taken permanent disability of 100%.
Even the PW.2 has stated 80% total disability for the petitioner.
It is true that the amputation was done below knee.
Hence under these circumstances, I just feel it proper to consider 40% disability for the petitioner.

21. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
a). Loss of future income:
The PW.1 has stated that he was doing agricultural work and vegetable business and earning Rs.40,000/ per month.
In this regard except Ex.P.13 the Patta passbook, he had not produced any other documents to show his actual income from agriculture work or from vegetable business.
Hence, in the absence of such documents, I just feel it proper to consider the notional income.
As on the date of accident the notional income can be fixed at Rs.14,500/.
The PW.1 had stated that he was aged about 43 years at the time of accident.
In (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.1012/20 this regard the PW.1 has got marked his Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.8 which reveals that the PW.1 was born in the year 1976.
Hence as per Ex.P.8 it is just and proper to consider the age of the petitioner as 44 years at the time of accident.
Thereby proper multiplier comes to "14".

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income as Rs.14,500 x 12 x 14 x 40/100 =
Rs.9,74,400/ under this head.
b). Pain and sufferings during treatment period: The petitioner has stated that he was admitted in hospital as inpatient.
In this regard he had got marked the Discharge summary as per Ex.P.9 which shows that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient from 12.01.2020 to 22.01.2020.
Hence under these circumstances, I just feel it proper to award Rs.25,000/ under this head.
c). Towards medical expenses: The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.10 which amounts to Rs.10,69,984/.

On perusal of Medical bills, it is noticed that Sl.No.64 and 65 are receipt vouchers for Rs.80,000/ and for Rs.40,000/ and it was paid for Sl.No.67 bill amount for Rs.1,20,000/, hence the said amount has to be deducted as it was taken twice.
The Sl. No.66 is the rehabilitation service proposal given by Ottobock for (SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.1012/20 Rs.3,40,000/ and it cannot be considered as the said amount was not paid by the petitioner.
There is no serious dispute with regard to other medical bills produced and marked by the petitioner.
Hence after deducting the said amount the petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,09,984/ under this head.

sentences.text:
5 d). Loss of income during laid up period:-
Admittedly the PW.1 as per available records could not do any work for about 1 month after the accident.
Hence, he is entitled for Rs.14,500/ under this head.

e). Loss of amenities and nutrition food:-
The PW.1 had not produced any documents to show that he had incurred amount towards amenities and nutritious food.
But looking into the period of treatment and the nature of injuries, I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this head.
f). Towards attendent charges and conveyance:
The PW.1 was admitted as inpatient for nearly 10 days.
In these days the petitioner has to look after by some body.
Hence under these circumstances I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this head.
g). Towards future medical expenses: The PW.2 has stated that the PW.1 required below knee (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.1012/20 prosthesis at the costs upto Rs.3,00,000/.
In this regard no supportive documents produced before this court.

Hence under these circumstances I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.50,000/
under this head.
22. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,93,884/ (Sixteen lakhs ninety three thousand eight hundred and eighty four only).
23. Regarding liability : The respondent No.1 has admitted the issuance of policy in the name of the respondent No.2.
It is true that the petitioner has proved that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry driver.
The said offending lorry was owned by the respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.1.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence I answered the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

Further as per my above findings on above and with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the petitioner is entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
As such I proceed to pass the following: (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.1012/20 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for Rs.16,93,884/ (Sixteen lakhs ninety three thousand eight hundred and eighty four only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a. (the interest awarded is not applicable to future medical expenses of Rs.50,000/) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
